+# Orders with two maximal absolute Hermite coefficients
+
+## Abstract
+
+The exact increasing enumeration of physicists Hermite orders with exactly two largest absolute coefficients.
+
+The order k and every exponent are natural numbers, including zero. The polynomial is exactly HermiteSignedMode.physicistsHermite over the rationals. Maximality compares absolute values over the entire coefficient row from zero through k, including the zero coefficients of the other parity. The index n of the enumeration starts at one. Its formula uses integer arithmetic, so the alternating summand is an ordinary signed integer.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Maximality in the complete original row).**
+
+$$\forall k:\mathbb{N}, \forall j:\mathbb{N}, \operatorname{IsAbsMax}\left(k, j\right) = ((j \le k) \land (\forall i:\mathbb{N}, (i \le k) \implies (\operatorname{abs}\left(\operatorname{coeff}\left(\operatorname{physicistsHermite}\left(k\right), i\right)\right) \le \operatorname{abs}\left(\operatorname{coeff}\left(\operatorname{physicistsHermite}\left(k\right), j\right)\right))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Analytic/Polynomial/HermiteAbsoluteTieOrders.IsAbsMax` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Mike Sheppard (2025). *Orders k of Hermite polynomials whose maximal coefficient in absolute value appears twice*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A381737/internal?rev=28>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+An exponent j is at most k and its absolute coefficient bounds the absolute coefficient at every exponent i at most k.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Exactly two distinct maxima).**
+
+$$\forall k:\mathbb{N}, \operatorname{HasExactlyTwo}\left(k\right) = (\exists u:\mathbb{N}, \exists v:\mathbb{N}, (u < v) \land (\forall j:\mathbb{N}, (\operatorname{IsAbsMax}\left(k, j\right)) \iff ((j = u) \lor (j = v))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Analytic/Polynomial/HermiteAbsoluteTieOrders.HasExactlyTwo` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Mike Sheppard (2025). *Orders k of Hermite polynomials whose maximal coefficient in absolute value appears twice*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A381737/internal?rev=28>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+There are exponents u less than v such that the maximizing exponents are precisely u and v. The equivalence for every natural j excludes both additional maxima and exponents outside the row.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The one-based source formula).**
+
+$$\forall n:\mathbb{N}, \operatorname{a}\left(n\right) = ((2) \cdot ((n:\mathbb{Z}))) \cdot (((n:\mathbb{Z})+2))+(((n:\mathbb{Z})+1)) \cdot ((-1)^{n+1})$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Analytic/Polynomial/HermiteAbsoluteTieOrders.a` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Mike Sheppard (2025). *Orders k of Hermite polynomials whose maximal coefficient in absolute value appears twice*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A381737/internal?rev=28>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+This is Conjecture 1 of OEIS A381737 revision 28. The natural index is cast to the integers before the additions and products. The exponent n+1 remains natural. The theorem uses only positive indices.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (The complete increasing exhaustive enumeration).**
+
+$$claim = ((\forall n:\mathbb{N}, (1 \le n) \implies (0 < \operatorname{a}\left(n\right))) \land ((\forall n:\mathbb{N}, \forall m:\mathbb{N}, (1 \le n) \implies ((n < m) \implies (\operatorname{a}\left(n\right) < \operatorname{a}\left(m\right)))) \land (\forall k:\mathbb{N}, (\operatorname{HasExactlyTwo}\left(k\right)) \iff (\exists n:\mathbb{N}, ((1 \le n) \land ((k:\mathbb{Z}) = \operatorname{a}\left(n\right))) \land (\forall m:\mathbb{N}, ((1 \le m) \land ((k:\mathbb{Z}) = \operatorname{a}\left(m\right))) \implies (m = n))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Analytic/Polynomial/HermiteAbsoluteTieOrders.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Mike Sheppard (2025). *Orders k of Hermite polynomials whose maximal coefficient in absolute value appears twice*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A381737/internal?rev=28>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Every positive-index value is positive; the values strictly increase with the index; and for every natural order k, exactly two maxima occur if and only if k equals the formula at one unique positive index. The displayed unique-index condition expands existence and uniqueness explicitly.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (Exact classification and enumeration).**
+
+$$(\forall n:\mathbb{N}, (1 \le n) \implies (0 < \operatorname{a}\left(n\right))) \land ((\forall n:\mathbb{N}, \forall m:\mathbb{N}, (1 \le n) \implies ((n < m) \implies (\operatorname{a}\left(n\right) < \operatorname{a}\left(m\right)))) \land (\forall k:\mathbb{N}, (\operatorname{HasExactlyTwo}\left(k\right)) \iff (\exists n:\mathbb{N}, ((1 \le n) \land ((k:\mathbb{Z}) = \operatorname{a}\left(n\right))) \land (\forall m:\mathbb{N}, ((1 \le m) \land ((k:\mathbb{Z}) = \operatorname{a}\left(m\right))) \implies (m = n)))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Analytic/Polynomial/HermiteAbsoluteTieOrders.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/oeis-a381737-hermite-absolute-ties` (proved) by `D5/S3/Analytic/Polynomial/HermiteAbsoluteTieOrders.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"oeis-a381737-hermite-absolute-ties","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Analytic/Polynomial/HermiteAbsoluteTieOrders.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Mike Sheppard (2025). *Orders k of Hermite polynomials whose maximal coefficient in absolute value appears twice*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A381737/internal?rev=28>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let w(k,r) be the original absolute signedCoeff at exponent k-2r, with 2r at most k. HermiteAbsoluteMode supplies positivity, the adjacent identity, maximality at mode(k), and strict decrease after that mode. Before the final adjacent pair, the threshold is strict: if r+1 is less than mode(k), then 4(r+1) is less than second(k-2(r+1)), where second(j)=(j+1)(j+2). The adjacent identity therefore gives w(k,r) less than w(k,r+1). A maximizing index must be mode(k) or mode(k)-1. Those two indices tie exactly when second(k-2r)=4r at r=mode(k), with r at least one. Conversely, any such equality forces r to be mode(k) and gives precisely those two maxima. The coefficient_cases and polynomial_coeff statements transfer the comparison to every exponent in the original polynomial row; zero parity coefficients cannot maximize because the mode weight is positive.
+
+Put j=k-2r. The tie equation is (j+1)(j+2)=4r. Its reduction modulo four forces j to be 4t+2 or 4t+3. In the first case k=8t squared+18t+8=a(2t+1); in the second, k=8t squared+22t+13=a(2t+2). Conversely, these formulas provide r=(4t+3)(t+1) and r=(4t+5)(t+1), respectively, satisfying the tie equation and 2r at most k. Every positive index is uniquely odd or even in these forms. The alternating power is either one or minus one; substitution shows that a(n+1)-a(n) is 2n+3 or 6n+9, both positive. Thus the enumeration is strictly increasing, and a(1)=8 makes every positive-index value positive. Strict increase gives the unique positive index for each qualifying order. No finite cutoff, rescaling of the coefficient row, or restriction to a subsequence is used.
+

+import D5.S3.Analytic.Polynomial.HermiteAbsoluteMode
+
+/-! Two absolute maxima in the original physicists Hermite coefficient row. -/
+
+namespace D5.S3.Analytic.Polynomial.HermiteAbsoluteTieOrders
+
+open HermiteSignedMode HermiteAbsoluteMode
+
+/-- Absolute maximality over every exponent from zero through the order. -/
+def IsAbsMax (k j : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  j ≤ k ∧ ∀ i, i ≤ k →
+    |(physicistsHermite k).coeff i| ≤ |(physicistsHermite k).coeff j|
+
+/-- Exactly two distinct maximizing exponents in the complete coefficient row. -/
+def HasExactlyTwo (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ u v : ℕ, u < v ∧ ∀ j : ℕ, IsAbsMax k j ↔ j = u ∨ j = v
+
+/-- The source formula, with a positive one-based natural index and integer arithmetic. -/
+def a (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
+  2 * (n : ℤ) * ((n : ℤ) + 2) + ((n : ℤ) + 1) * (-1 : ℤ) ^ (n + 1)
+
+/-- Positive, strictly increasing, and exhaustive one-based enumeration. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → 0 < a n) ∧
+  (∀ n m : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → n < m → a n < a m) ∧
+  ∀ k : ℕ, HasExactlyTwo k ↔ ∃! n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ (k : ℤ) = a n
+
+private theorem max_iff_weight (k j : ℕ) :
+    IsAbsMax k j ↔ ∃ r : ℕ, 2 * r ≤ k ∧ j = k - 2 * r ∧
+      weight k r = weight k (mode k) := by
+  have hm := (mode_rises k).1
+  have hp := weight_pos k (mode k) hm
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    have htop := h.2 (k - 2 * mode k) (Nat.sub_le _ _)
+    rw [polynomial_coeff k _ (Nat.sub_le _ _), polynomial_coeff k j h.1] at htop
+    change weight k (mode k) ≤ |signedCoeff k j| at htop
+    rcases coefficient_cases k j with hz | ⟨r, hr, hj, hw⟩
+    · rw [hz] at htop
+      linarith
+    · exact ⟨r, hr, hj, le_antisymm (weight_le_mode k r hr) (hw ▸ htop)⟩
+  · rintro ⟨r, hr, rfl, he⟩
+    refine ⟨Nat.sub_le _ _, ?_⟩
+    intro i hi
+    rw [polynomial_coeff k i hi, polynomial_coeff k _ (Nat.sub_le _ _)]
+    change |signedCoeff k i| ≤ weight k r
+    rw [he]
+    rcases coefficient_cases k i with hz | ⟨s, hs, hj, hw⟩
+    · rw [hz]; exact hp.le
+    · rw [hw]; exact weight_le_mode k s hs
+
+private theorem strict_before (k r : ℕ) (hr : r + 1 < mode k) :
+    weight k r < weight k (r + 1) := by
+  have hm := mode_rises k
+  have hmd := hm.1
+  have hmc := hm.2
+  have hdom : 2 * (r + 1) ≤ k := by omega
+  have hcomp := second_mono (show k - 2 * mode k ≤ k - 2 * (r + 1) by omega)
+  have ht : 4 * (r + 1) < second (k - 2 * (r + 1)) := by omega
+  have htq : (4 * (r + 1) : ℚ) < second (k - 2 * (r + 1)) := by exact_mod_cast ht
+  have hw := weight_pos k r (by omega)
+  have he := adjacent k r hdom
+  have hd : (0 : ℚ) < 4 * (r + 1) := by positivity
+  nlinarith
+
+private theorem equal_mode_indices (k r : ℕ) (hr : 2 * r ≤ k)
+    (he : weight k r = weight k (mode k)) :
+    r = mode k ∨ r + 1 = mode k := by
+  have hle : r ≤ mode k := by
+    by_contra h
+    have := weight_lt_mode k r hr (by omega)
+    linarith
+  by_cases h : r + 1 < mode k
+  · have hs := strict_before k r h
+    have ht := weight_le_mode k (r + 1) (by have := (mode_rises k).1; omega)
+    linarith
+  · omega
+
+private theorem adjacent_equal (k r : ℕ) (hr : 2 * (r + 1) ≤ k) :
+    weight k r = weight k (r + 1) ↔
+      second (k - 2 * (r + 1)) = 4 * (r + 1) := by
+  have he := adjacent k r hr
+  have hp := weight_pos k r (by omega)
+  have hd : (0 : ℚ) < 4 * (r + 1) := by positivity
+  constructor
+  · intro hh
+    rw [← hh] at he
+    have : (second (k - 2 * (r + 1)) : ℚ) = 4 * (r + 1) := by nlinarith
+    exact_mod_cast this
+  · intro hh
+    have : (second (k - 2 * (r + 1)) : ℚ) = 4 * (r + 1) := by exact_mod_cast hh
+    rw [this] at he
+    nlinarith
+
+private theorem tie_is_mode (k r : ℕ) (hk : 2 * r ≤ k)
+    (he : second (k - 2 * r) = 4 * r) : r = mode k := by
+  have hle : r ≤ mode k := le_mode ⟨hk, he.ge⟩
+  have hm := mode_rises k
+  have hmd := hm.1
+  have hmc := hm.2
+  have hc := second_mono (show k - 2 * mode k ≤ k - 2 * r by omega)
+  omega
+
+private theorem tie_characterization (k : ℕ) :
+    HasExactlyTwo k ↔ ∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ 2 * r ≤ k ∧
+      second (k - 2 * r) = 4 * r := by
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨u, v, huv, h⟩
+    obtain ⟨r, hr, hu, her⟩ := (max_iff_weight k u).mp ((h u).mpr (Or.inl rfl))
+    obtain ⟨s, hs, hv, hes⟩ := (max_iff_weight k v).mp ((h v).mpr (Or.inr rfl))
+    have hri := equal_mode_indices k r hr her
+    have hsi := equal_mode_indices k s hs hes
+    have hsr : s < r := by omega
+    have hrr : r = mode k := by omega
+    have hss : s + 1 = r := by omega
+    refine ⟨r, by omega, hr, ?_⟩
+    have heq : weight k s = weight k (s + 1) := by rw [hss, hrr]; exact hes
+    have ht := (adjacent_equal k s (by omega)).mp heq
+    simpa only [hss] using ht
+  · rintro ⟨r, hr, hk, he⟩
+    have hm := tie_is_mode k r hk he
+    have heq : weight k (r - 1) = weight k r := by
+      have hh : r - 1 + 1 = r := by omega
+      simpa only [hh] using (adjacent_equal k (r - 1) (by omega)).mpr (by simpa only [hh] using he)
+    refine ⟨k - 2 * r, k - 2 * (r - 1), by omega, ?_⟩
+    intro j
+    rw [max_iff_weight]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨s, hs, hj, hes⟩
+      have hi := equal_mode_indices k s hs hes
+      rcases hi with hi | hi
+      · left; omega
+      · right; omega
+    · rintro (rfl | rfl)
+      · exact ⟨r, hk, rfl, by rw [← hm]⟩
+      · exact ⟨r - 1, by omega, rfl, by rw [← hm]; exact heq⟩
+
+private theorem a_odd (t : ℕ) :
+    a (2 * t + 1) = 8 * (t : ℤ) ^ 2 + 18 * (t : ℤ) + 8 := by
+  unfold a
+  rw [show 2 * t + 1 + 1 = 2 * (t + 1) by omega, pow_mul]
+  norm_num
+  ring
+
+private theorem a_even (t : ℕ) :
+    a (2 * t + 2) = 8 * (t : ℤ) ^ 2 + 22 * (t : ℤ) + 13 := by
+  unfold a
+  rw [show 2 * t + 2 + 1 = 2 * (t + 1) + 1 by omega, pow_add, pow_mul]
+  norm_num
+  ring
+
+private theorem a_strictMono : StrictMono a := by
+  apply strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ
+  intro n
+  have hpow : (-1 : ℤ) ^ (n + 1 + 1) = -((-1 : ℤ) ^ (n + 1)) := by
+    rw [pow_succ]; ring
+  unfold a
+  rw [hpow]
+  push_cast
+  rcases neg_one_pow_eq_or ℤ (n + 1) with h | h <;> rw [h] <;> nlinarith
+
+private theorem a_positive (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : 0 < a n := by
+  have hone : a 1 = 8 := by norm_num [a]
+  have hh := a_strictMono.monotone hn
+  rw [hone] at hh
+  omega

+private theorem tie_orders (k : ℕ) :
+    (∃ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r ∧ 2 * r ≤ k ∧ second (k - 2 * r) = 4 * r) ↔
+      ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ (k : ℤ) = a n := by
+  constructor

+    let j := k - 2 * r
+    have hjk : k = j + 2 * r := by dsimp [j]; omega
+    have he' : (j + 1) * (j + 2) = 4 * r := he
+    have hmod := congrArg (fun x : ℕ => x % 4) he'
+    have hrem : j % 4 = 0 ∨ j % 4 = 1 ∨ j % 4 = 2 ∨ j % 4 = 3 := by omega
+    have hrem' : j % 4 = 2 ∨ j % 4 = 3 := by
+      rcases hrem with h | h | h | h
+      · norm_num [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, h] at hmod
+      · norm_num [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, h] at hmod
+      · exact Or.inl h
+      · exact Or.inr h

+      refine ⟨2 * t + 1, by omega, ?_⟩
+      rw [a_odd, hv]
+      push_cast
+      ring
+    · have hj : j = 4 * t + 3 := by dsimp [t]; omega
+      rw [hj] at hjk he'
+      have hv : k = 8 * t ^ 2 + 22 * t + 13 := by nlinarith [he']
+      refine ⟨2 * t + 2, by omega, ?_⟩
+      rw [a_even, hv]
+      push_cast
+      ring
+  · rintro ⟨n, hn, he⟩
+    let t := (n - 1) / 2
+    have hsplit : n = 2 * t + 1 ∨ n = 2 * t + 2 := by dsimp [t]; omega
+    rcases hsplit with h | h
+    · rw [h, a_odd] at he
+      have hv : k = 8 * t ^ 2 + 18 * t + 8 := by exact_mod_cast he
+      refine ⟨(4 * t + 3) * (t + 1), by nlinarith, ?_, ?_⟩
+      · nlinarith [hv]
+      · have hsum : k = 2 * ((4 * t + 3) * (t + 1)) + (4 * t + 2) := by nlinarith [hv]
+        have hj : k - 2 * ((4 * t + 3) * (t + 1)) = 4 * t + 2 := by omega
+        rw [hj]
+        unfold second
+        ring
+    · rw [h, a_even] at he
+      have hv : k = 8 * t ^ 2 + 22 * t + 13 := by exact_mod_cast he
+      refine ⟨(4 * t + 5) * (t + 1), by nlinarith, ?_, ?_⟩
+      · nlinarith [hv]
+      · have hsum : k = 2 * ((4 * t + 5) * (t + 1)) + (4 * t + 3) := by nlinarith [hv]
+        have hj : k - 2 * ((4 * t + 5) * (t + 1)) = 4 * t + 3 := by omega
+        rw [hj]
+        unfold second
+        ring

+theorem result : claim := by
+  refine ⟨a_positive, fun n m _ h => a_strictMono h, ?_⟩
+  intro k
+  rw [tie_characterization, tie_orders]
+  constructor
+  · rintro ⟨n, hn, he⟩

+    exact a_strictMono.injective (hem.symm.trans he)
+  · rintro ⟨n, hn, _⟩
+    exact ⟨n, hn⟩

+# The complete A381737 Conjecture 1 enumeration
+
+## Problem
+
+OEIS A381737, revision 28, by Mike Sheppard (2025), names the sequence:
+
+> Orders k of Hermite polynomials whose maximal coefficient in absolute value appears twice.
+
+Its Formula field states:
+
+> Conjecture 1: a(n) = 2*n*(n + 2) + (n + 1)*(-1)^(n+1).
+
+The offset is 1,1. Let $H_k$ be the physicists Hermite polynomial, with the
+original coefficients represented by `HermiteSignedMode.physicistsHermite`
+over the rationals. For natural $k$ and $j$, write
+
+$$
+M(k,j)\iff j\le k\ \land\ \forall i\le k,\quad
+|[x^i]H_k|\le |[x^j]H_k|.
+$$
+
+Exactly two maxima means that there exist $u<v$ such that, for every natural
+$j$, $M(k,j)$ holds if and only if $j=u$ or $j=v$. The entire row from zero
+through $k$ is compared, including zero coefficients of the other parity.
+For every positive natural index, define the integer value
+
+$$
+a(n)=2n(n+2)+(n+1)(-1)^{n+1}.
+$$
+
+The complete assertion is that $a(n)>0$ for every $n\ge1$, that
+$a(n)<a(m)$ whenever $1\le n<m$, and that for every natural order $k$,
+including zero, exactly two maxima occur if and only if there is exactly one
+$n\ge1$ with $(k:\mathbb Z)=a(n)$. The additions and products in the formula
+are integer operations; $n+1$ in the exponent is natural. There is no finite
+cutoff or asymptotic qualification.
+
+## Motivation
+
+This dossier concerns the whole external Conjecture 1, preregistered at
+https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/25855#issuecomment-6590328488.
+The full-row meaning follows the source name and its physicists $H_8$
+example. The neighboring absolute-mode result supplies coefficient
+maximality, while the tie classification and enumeration identify every
+qualifying order. Conjectures 2 and 3 are outside this resolution.
+
+## Gap
+
+The Library note identifies revision 28, the Name and Formula fields and
+the one-based offset. Programs and finite examples do not supply the
+universal enumeration. The needed relation is an exact tie criterion for
+the original coefficient row, followed by an exhaustive solution of that
+criterion and uniqueness of the positive index. The source locator does
+not certify worldwide current openness or priority, and no such claim is
+made here.
+
+## Route
+
+For $2r\le k$, let $w(k,r)$ be the absolute value of the original coefficient
+at exponent $k-2r$. The existing absolute-mode results give positivity, the
+adjacent coefficient identity, maximality at $\operatorname{mode}(k)$ and
+strict decrease beyond that index. The strict threshold before the last
+adjacent pair restricts a maximizing index to
+$\operatorname{mode}(k)$ or $\operatorname{mode}(k)-1$. A tie occurs exactly
+when, for some $r\ge1$ with $2r\le k$,
+
+$$
+(k-2r+1)(k-2r+2)=4r.
+$$
+
+Conversely this equality forces $r=\operatorname{mode}(k)$ and precisely two
+maxima. The coefficient extraction theorem transfers this statement to
+every exponent in the full polynomial row; parity zeros cannot maximize a
+positive mode weight.
+
+Put $j=k-2r$. The equality forces $j=4t+2$ or $j=4t+3$. These give,
+respectively, $k=8t^2+18t+8=a(2t+1)$ and
+$k=8t^2+22t+13=a(2t+2)$, and both families supply a valid $r$.
+Every positive index is of exactly one of these forms. The adjacent integer
+difference $a(n+1)-a(n)$ is $2n+3$ or $6n+9$, hence positive; $a(1)=8$.
+Strict increase supplies uniqueness as well as positivity and exhaustion.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+A positive index with a nonpositive value, a pair $1\le n<m$ with
+$a(n)\ge a(m)$, or a natural order at which exactly two full-row absolute
+maxima disagree with the unique-positive-index condition would falsify the
+complete event. A finite list, a different Hermite normalization or a
+restriction to nonzero coefficients cannot replace this criterion.
+
+## Evidence

+`D5/S3/Analytic/Polynomial/HermiteAbsoluteTieOrders.result` proves the complete
+`claim`, whose definitions retain the original row, exactly two distinct
+maximizers, every positive index and every natural order. Its owning Scribe
